items.snippet: The integration of artificial intelligence across global financial markets repre...
items.raw_snippet: The integration of artificial intelligence across global financial markets represents one of the most profound structural shifts in modern economic history. From multinational technology conglomerates and financial institutions to market infrastructure providers, market participants are re-architecting their strategies to harness predictive modeling, machine learning, and natural language processing. While artificial intelligence serves as a major catalyst for productivity enhancement, corporate earnings expansion, and accelerated price discovery, it simultaneously introduces new complexities to market microstructure. As automated execution and algorithmic decision-making become standard across global exchanges, the financial ecosystem faces unprecedented questions regarding market volatility, valuation sustainability, and systemic risk oversight. As financial markets become increasingly automated, the balance between market efficiency and market stability will depend on the ability of institutional investors, corporate leaders, and regulatory bodies to implement robust risk controls, maintain oversight of automated models, and adapt to an accelerated financial landscape.

items.snippet: # The AI advantage is moving into the physical economy. Industrial ecosystems wi...
items.raw_snippet: # The AI advantage is moving into the physical economy. Industrial ecosystems will be more important in the next phase of artificial intelligence. As AI expands into the physical world, the geography of start-up advantage is becoming more complicated. As AI expands into the physical world, the geography of start-up advantage is becoming more complicated© FT/Andrew Petrie/ChatGPT. For the past few years, the easiest answer to the question “where should an AI start-up build?” was wherever the leading models, research talent and computing infrastructure were concentrated. But as AI expands into the physical world, via robots, factories, energy systems and infrastructure, the geography of start-up advantage is becoming more complicated. Yet for companies building AI systems that operate in the physical world, models are only one part of the equation. Industrial ecosystems may therefore become more important to the next phase of AI than conventional start-up rankings suggest.
